fixes.explanation: Priests never come into this scene. The father says he begged Jesus' disciples to drive the spirit out. And then he says they were unable. Then he cries out to Jesus in front of the crowd.
After His “How long must I remain with you…” line, Jesus tells the father, “Bring your son here.” No speech about it. Jesus calls the boy to Himself. Short and clear, and the father has his answer.
Jesus doesn't send the father home. He says, “Bring your son here.” The boy is going to be brought to Him. Jesus wants to deal with this face to face.

Luke says Jesus healed the boy “…and gave him back to his father.” Think about who that father is: a man who called this boy his only child. I think this is the line to sit with for a second. The boy is well, and Jesus gives him back to his dad.

The text says the opposite of false. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and “…gave him back to his father.” The father who begged for his only child gets him back. That's what Luke tells us.
Money isn't what they're arguing about. The text says the argument was about which of them would be the greatest. It's about rank, not a wallet. Luke doesn't mention money anywhere in this scene.
No travel plans here. Luke says the argument was about which of them would be the greatest. The text doesn't mention a next town at all. It's all about who's on top.

Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, “…had a little child stand beside Him.” He doesn't start with a lecture. He sets a child right there where everyone can see. Then He speaks to them about welcoming that child in His name.
A tax collector isn't in this scene. Jesus has a little child stand beside Him. That's who He brings in when the argument has started among the disciples. And that child is the picture He uses next.

Jesus says, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me…” Then He adds, “…and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me.” So welcoming that child in His name connects straight to Him. That's a big deal for a little child standing right beside Him.

John, one of Jesus' disciples, says, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name…” The man was doing it in Jesus' name, and John says that right up front. So the disciples spotted a man doing the very thing they had struggled with earlier. And John goes on to say what they did about it.
John, one of Jesus' disciples, doesn't mention healing the blind. He says they saw someone driving out demons in Jesus' name. Then he says they tried to stop him. Healing the blind never comes up.
Money isn't John's complaint. He says they tried to stop the man “…because he does not accompany us.” That's the reason John gives. The text says nothing about payment.
John never says the man was a Pharisee. His reason is that the man “…does not accompany us.” That's the reason he gives. The man simply wasn't traveling with them.

Close, but that's not Jesus' word. He says, “…whoever is not against you is for you.” John said the man does not accompany them, and Jesus still says not to stop him. The word Jesus uses is “against.”
